scenes.say: Ever wonder why Go doesn't need an implements keyword for interfaces?

scenes.label: Method Set
scenes.sub: A type matches an interface if it has all the interface's methods.
scenes.say: In Go, a type matches an interface if it has all the methods the interface requires.
Here, File has a Read method. So it automatically satisfies the Reader interface—no extra code needed.
This keeps your code flexible, decoupled, and free from boilerplate. You can swap in any type that fits the interface.

scenes.question: How do you declare a type implements an interface?
scenes.wrong: You use an explicit implements keyword.
scenes.right: You just match the method set—no explicit declaration needed.
scenes.say: Don't say you use an explicit implements keyword. In Go, just matching the method set is enough.
